description:
verify_dns_name(cert: &Certificate, ...) and verify_mailbox(cert: &Certificate, ...) take &x509_cert::Certificate directly in the public signature. The pkix-identity crate does not re-export Certificate, so callers must:

  pkix-identity = "0.1"
  x509-cert     = "..."   // must match what pkix-identity uses

If x509-cert cuts a major version, every pkix-identity dependent must coordinate the upgrade in lockstep, even if their direct use of x509-cert is only via pkix-identity. This is the textbook 'public dep' problem.

Mitigations (pick one before 1.0):

1. Re-export: `pub use x509_cert;` at the crate root, so callers can do `use pkix_identity::x509_cert::Certificate;` and stay coupled to whatever pkix-identity is built against.

2. Trait abstraction: define a small `IdentityCertSource` trait that exposes only the SAN-extension-bytes accessor pkix-identity actually needs. Implement it for x509_cert::Certificate (gated by an x509-cert feature). This lets callers using a different cert representation (yasna, picky, custom parser) plug in.

3. Take &[u8] DER directly and parse internally. Re-parsing per call is the wrong default for the batch-validation pattern (non-negotiable #6), so this is the worst option.

Most likely (1) is sufficient. The decision is whether to also offer (2) for callers wanting representation-independence.

This is currently the *only* upstream type in the public surface. der::Decode (used in tests) is on the std::error::Error blanket impl; ObjectIdentifier and Any are not in the public surface.

Severity P2: adding a re-export is non-breaking, so this is fixable later — but only by the maintainer remembering to add it; calling it out for explicit 1.0-gate decision.
title: Public Certificate type from x509-cert leaks upstream major-version pin into pkix-identity API
